These results show that specialist tools and language-level policy optimization can extend the clinical and general EEG capabilities of a single locally executable model while preserving local inference and traceable tool use.

Machine Learning.title: Same Path, Less Time: Training-Free Fast Execution of Vision-Language-Action Models under Inference Latency
Machine Learning.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models predict chunks of future actions, yet deployed robots waste time in two ways that are independent of model capability: they halt while the next chunk is inferred, and they move at the speed of slow, cautious demonstrations. Existing remedies remove one loss each, and stacking them fails, because asynchrony and speed-up each change the correspondence between planned progress and executed motion. We present Path-preserving Time Scaling (PTS), a training-free execution layer for frozen action-chunking policies built on one principle: the robot's motion is a time reparameterization of a reference path, and the path changes only in response to new observations. A path layer decodes every replan deterministically in one step and enters it at the progress consumed during inference. A time layer sums the planned increments, keeps the arm at 1x while the gripper moves, and caps the rate by the actuator's linear range and by chunk feasibility under latency. We show that misaligned entry and stochastic sampling add a bias and a variance to the continuation error, and derive a break-even success rate that states when speeding up pays off. On LIBERO with two frozen VLAs under injected inference latency, PTS raises task throughput over the strongest deployable baseline by 33% for pi0.5 and 104% for SmolVLA while matching or improving the success rate, is best on all six model-suite combinations, and exceeds zero-latency 1x execution. Against asynchronous 1x execution with the same one-step decoder, the time layer alone adds 28% and 38%. On LIBERO-Dynamic it improves on stop-and-wait execution by 38% and is comparable to asynchronous 1x execution.

Machine Learning.title: Benign population landscapes do not transfer to empirical risk minimization in nonsmooth optimization
Machine Learning.summary: Benign landscapes provide a geometric explanation for the success of iterative methods on nonconvex problems arising in data science. The landscape is benign if every local minimizer is global and every other critical point is a strict saddle. For methods that avoid strict saddles, convergence to a critical point therefore implies convergence to a global minimizer. For smooth stochastic optimization, a common strategy for establishing such landscapes proceeds in two steps: $(i)$ establish benign geometry for the population objective---which is often easier to analyze---and $(ii)$ transfer this geometry to the empirical objective using concentration of gradients and Hessians. Recent work has extended saddle-point avoidance guarantees to weakly convex nonsmooth optimization through the notion of active strict saddles. We show, however, that benign population geometry need not transfer to empirical objectives in this setting. Specifically, for robust phase retrieval with Gaussian measurements---a well-studied and highly structured problem---the population objective is benign. Nevertheless, the empirical objective has sharp spurious local minima with probability bounded away from zero as the sample size tends to infinity. This asymptotic probability lower bound is independent of the dimension.

Machine Learning.title: Toward Executable Multi-framework Front-end Code Generation with Self-Correction
Machine Learning.summary: Generating codes from UI screenshots has recently benefited from MLLMs, yet existing methods centered on HTML targets and transfer poorly to multi-frameworks such as React, Vue, and Angular. However, unlike HTML, which does not entail compilation issues, generating executable code in multi-framework settings is more challenging due to framework-specific differences in syntax and failure modes, as well as the need to maintain global consistency across files. To address this problem, we study executable multi-framework front-end code generation and propose MESCoder, a tree-structured self-corrective generation framework. Our method first extracts a structural scaffold from the screenshot and then constructs sub-trees and assembly relations step by step, transforming large project generation into a sequence of localized decisions. On top of this scaffold, we introduce a unified Project Agent that continuously revises its own partial project under runtime sandbox feedback and dynamically chooses between local repair and cluster level repair. For training, we adopt a two-stage strategy that first initializes the policy offline to learn basic multi-framework generation and repair priors, and then refines it with online reinforcement learning to optimize long horizon executability and final page quality. The resulting framework models multi-framework executability as a conditioned project state transition process and improves the stability and quality of complex front end generation through self correction. Experiments show that our method improves executability, while narrowing the visual-fidelity gap to HTML-based generation. Code is available at https://github.com/leo-lilinxiao/MESCoder.

Machine Learning.title: Information-Theoretic Design of Sparse Autoencoder-Based Steering
Machine Learning.summary: Sparse autoencoder (SAE)-based activation steering is a lightweight approach for modifying the behavior of large language models (LLMs) by adding small vectors to hidden states during inference. However, designing effective steering interventions remains challenging. In this work, we develop an information-theoretic framework for analyzing SAE activations through empirical feature-firing distributions. The central object of the framework is the Jensen--Shannon divergence (JSD) between such firing distributions, which quantifies how far a generated or intervened state deviates from a dataset-induced target distribution. Based on an analytic divergence response for virtually shifted states, we construct steering vectors toward the target firing distribution. The same divergence can also be used to monitor deviation from another empirical distribution, such as a general valid-language distribution. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the steering in a question-mode generation task study. We further use teacher-forced pulse experiments to show that local interventions induce structured downstream JSD responses in later layers, and apply the framework to a safety-related target--contrast response setting for feature analysis.

Machine Learning.title: M$^3$: Reframing Training Measures for Discretized Physical Simulations
Machine Learning.summary: Neural surrogate models for physical simulations are trained on discretized samples of continuous domains, where the induced empirical measure leads to uneven supervision, biasing optimization and causing spatial inconsistencies in physical fidelity. To mitigate this measure-induced bias, we propose M$^3$ (Multi-scale Morton Measure), a scalable framework that balances training measures by partitioning space according to physical variation and allocating supervision across multiple scales. Applied to three industrial-scale datasets with diverse discretizations, M$^3$ consistently improves predictions in the continuous physical domain, achieving up to 4.7$\times$ lower error in large-scale volumetric cases. These gains persist under aggressive subsampling (160M $\rightarrow$ 16M $\rightarrow$ 1.6M points), where M$^3$-trained models outperform those trained on higher-resolution data, reducing physics-weighted relative $L_2$ error by 3--4$\times$ and the corresponding MSE by up to 13$\times$. These results highlight data distribution as a key factor in operator learning and position M$^3$ as a scalable, data-efficient approach for physically consistent modeling. Code is available at https://github.com/PhysDataRefine/M3.

Machine Learning.title: State-Augmented Learning for Post-Deployment Adaptation of Coexisting O-RAN Applications
Machine Learning.summary: Fixed control policies in Open RAN can require retraining when service requirements, traffic loads, or interacting applications change. We propose ATTUNE, a state-augmented learning method for an energy saving application that coexists with a learned mobility load balancing application under a service constraint. ATTUNE conditions the energy saving policy on a Lagrange multiplier and updates this scalar during operation using measured service degradation, while keeping both applications' network parameters fixed. To train a single policy across service requirements, ATTUNE samples target service levels uniformly and maps them to multipliers through an adaptive table. This procedure accounts for policy-dependent multiplier responses and improves energy savings compared with training over a widened fixed multiplier range. We characterize the induced distribution of service levels and the convergence and fluctuations of the online update. An exact finite-window identity establishes convergence of average measured degradation to the target when the projection corrections vanish on average. Simulations show that a single ATTUNE policy achieves energy savings comparable to policies trained separately for each service requirement. It adapts to changes in the target, load, and partner application without retraining, increases energy savings at light load, and maintains target tracking for separately trained application pairs. No statistically significant increase in cell switching is detected in the evaluated comparisons.
Machine Learning.comment: submitted to IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

Machine Learning.title: RATSIFT: Resolution-Adaptive Transformer for Solar Irradiance Forecasting and Temporal Downscaling
Machine Learning.summary: Accurate forecasting and temporal downscaling of solar irradiance is critical for reliable renewable energy integration and grid management. Traditional methods often struggle to capture rapid irradiance variability. In this work, we develop a Transformer-based architecture for simultaneous forecasting and temporal downscaling. The model takes input data at arbitrary resolutions and generates outputs at any resolutions represented within the training data, leveraging both global and local contextual information. To improve training efficiency, a genetic algorithm-based optimization framework is implemented to identify suitable model hyperparameters, while reducing the computational cost of exhaustive grid search. The effectiveness of the proposed model is shown by analyzing real data in Dallas, Texas. The proposed model achieved root mean square error (RMSE) values of 28.785, 29.544, 30.157, 32.132~W/m\(^2\) for 15-, 30-, 60-minute, and irregularly spaced global input and producing forecast at 5-minutes resolution, respectively. Furthermore, this model produced reliable uncertainty estimates, exhibiting wider prediction intervals for high-resolution inputs during volatile solar conditions, whereas coarser-resolution inputs result in narrower intervals and significantly lower training time and computational cost. Our approach provides a scalable and efficient framework for multi-resolution solar irradiance forecasting and temporal downscaling, suitable for practical energy forecasting and grid management applications.

Machine Learning.title: SSPE: Robust Sequential Staypoint Extraction in Degraded Trajectory Data
Machine Learning.summary: Extracting semantically meaningful staypoints from raw trajectory streams is a foundational prerequisite for mobility analytics. However, real-world trajectory data is frequently degraded by severe spatial noise and protracted temporal dropouts. Classic threshold-based extraction methods, such as the widely adopted sliding-window algorithm, are highly sensitive to these anomalies, routinely fracturing continuous stationary episodes into disjointed fragments. To overcome this limitation, we propose the Sequential Staypoint Extraction (SSPE) algorithm. SSPE employs a resilient, state-driven architecture that replaces static spatial anchors with a dynamic centroid and introduces an $n$-step lookahead heuristic to structurally tolerate transient coordinate drift. Concurrently, it utilizes temporal bridging mechanisms to prevent artificial fragmentation during prolonged signal loss. Since optimal extraction parameters vary significantly across datasets, we further introduce a fully unsupervised, consensus-based parameter estimation framework. This framework derives baseline statistical scales directly from the raw trajectory data and identifies the optimal parameter configuration by maximizing structural agreement, thereby eliminating the reliance on annotated ground truth. We evaluate SSPE on the ExtraSensory dataset, a real-world mobility corpus with manually verified ground-truth staypoints, against the sliding-window implementation of Trackintel, one of the most widely adopted extraction baselines in the field. Empirical results demonstrate that SSPE achieves superior accuracy, yielding higher F1-scores while simultaneously improving computational efficiency over this standard.

Machine Learning.title: Bernoulli On-Policy Distillation: Don't Ignore High-Confidence Student Tokens
Machine Learning.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model on its own trajectories using token-level supervision from a stronger teacher. We show that standard sampled reverse-KL OPD systematically suppresses updates to high-confidence tokens, such that their weak gradient contribution does not necessarily imply weak or uninformative teacher supervision. We introduce Bernoulli On-Policy Distillation (Bernoulli OPD), which directly matches the teacher and student probabilities for that token. This yields a bounded probability space correction that preserves teacher-student disagreement while avoiding the additional confidence-dependent suppression induced by vanilla OPD. Fixed-rollout analyses show that Bernoulli OPD substantially restores optimization signal to high-confidence tokens while remaining sensitive to teacher-student disagreement. We further analyze the resulting model behavior through confidence distributions, answer calibration, policy movement, and training dynamics, showing that Bernoulli OPD's gains cannot be explained simply by longer reasoning, larger optimization steps, or more uniform imitation of the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/duterscmy/Bernoulli-OPD.

Machine Learning.title: HyVox: Rethinking Low-Power Voice Intelligence towards Neuromorphic-von Neumann Edge Computing
Machine Learning.summary: We present HyVox, a hybrid neuromorphic--von Neumann system for low-energy open-set speaker identification under tight energy budgets. HyVox splits the workload at the speaker embedding. A neuromorphic processor embeds the speech with sparse, event-driven computation, and a von Neumann microcontroller holds the speaker gallery and makes every decision: it scores queries by cosine similarity, rejects unknown speakers, and enrolls new users by writing a prototype, with no weight update. On the neuromorphic processor, a hierarchical temporal abstraction (HTA) SNN backbone learns a synaptic time constant per leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron, allocating 832 neurons across fast, medium, and slow timescales. A 32-neuron spiking embedding extractor (SEE), pretrained on episodes that each enroll new speakers and reject outsiders, turns the backbone output into an embedding for speakers unseen in training; its 32 spike counts are the only interface between the two processors. To fit the chip's synapse and integer budgets, we compress the backbone 6.5x to 29.0k synapses, train it for integer bit-shift dynamics, and fine-tune it with chip-accurate spiking training (CAST). CAST trains through a differentiable replica of the chip's integer neuron update, derived from its cycle-accurate simulator, so that gradient descent optimizes the exact weights and thresholds the chip runs; it doubles the top-1 accuracy of the mapped backbone on unseen speakers. On 20 Common Voice households of unseen speakers, HyVox reaches 99.6\% top-1 and 5.5\% rejection EER with 2 members and 94.9\% and 13.2\% with 20, and the network deployed on the neuromorphic chip matches its trained model. Each inference on a 3-s window takes 0.96 s and 1.63 mJ of dynamic energy, 42\% lower latency than the fastest embedded ANN baseline and 13.5x less dynamic and 5.8x less total energy than the most energy-efficient one.

Machine Learning.title: Minimal Superior Penalties: Characterising and Calibrating Decision-Aware Proper Scoring Rules
Machine Learning.summary: Training a classifier means letting a validation metric decide which model is kept and when training stops. A natural requirement on that metric is superiority: every correctly classified forecast should score better than every incorrectly classified one, however close the underlying probabilities are. Neither the Brier score nor the logarithmic score satisfies this on its own. We show that superiority is governed by the separation between two endpoints -- the supremum of the score on correct predictions and the infimum on incorrect predictions -- and derive both in closed form for each score. Their difference is the infimal penalty, the greatest lower bound on the penalty needed to restore superiority. Prior work restores superiority with a penalty calibrated from the first endpoint alone; for the Brier base, our infimal penalty is smaller than that published penalty by a factor ranging from 4.00 at three classes to 2.11 at twenty. We further embed the published and infimal penalties in a one-parameter family and show that, under a single-valued tie convention, every member of the family is strictly proper. In a pre-specified two-dataset case study, mean selected-model macro-F1 rises with the penalty in the reported ten-class regimes, though not distinguishably from noise once seed/selection-mode nesting is accounted for; a fifth regime at forty-seven classes does not reproduce even this descriptive pattern. The intended no-superiority baseline is algebraically a rescaling of the family under test, so the experiment cannot attribute the observed pattern specifically to superiority. When superiority itself is the objective, any penalty strictly above the infimal value suffices; choosing a larger penalty is a separate calibration trade-off rather than a requirement for the guarantee.

Machine Learning.title: Complete Donor-Set Guidance for Frozen Diffusion Docking Models
Machine Learning.summary: Metalloprotein docking requires a ligand pose to satisfy both global pocket fit and the identity and geometry of metal-coordinating atoms. General-purpose diffusion docking models do not explicitly condition generation on externally specified complete ligand donor sets, and their predicted poses can exhibit incorrect metal-donor relationships. Metal-aware models address coordination during training and generation; here we ask whether external donor information can correct already-trained general-purpose models without retraining. We propose Complete-Identity Contract Guidance (CICG), which applies a supplied complete donor set through translation, rotation, and torsion updates, and Historical Contract Transfer (HCT), which supplies donor identities from earlier complexes at compatible receptor sites. We compare HCT with trajectory-local controls retaining the historical donor count with or without elemental composition. On 86 assessable HCT-covered queries, HCT-guided CICG increases frozen-confidence-selected joint success from 21.5% to 36.6% on SurfDock and from 25.0% to 34.9% on DiffDock-L. The joint criterion requires correct global ligand placement, complete native donor recovery, coordination geometry, preserved stereochemistry, and absence of fatal receptor clashes. Composition-matched guidance reaches 33.14% and 34.30%, leaving the additional benefit of fixed historical membership unresolved. Our results therefore support donor-set guidance as a conditional correction for frozen docking models, while identifying donor-source reliability and physical-quality preservation as the main barriers to broader use.
Machine Learning.comment: 38 pages including appendices, 4 figures. Hyunwoo Kim and Insoo Park contributed equally

Machine Learning.title: Auditing a Model-Hub Benchmark: Data Quality, Training Budgets, and Side Information in HuggingBench
Machine Learning.summary: Benchmarks built from model hubs combine interaction data, knowledge graphs (KGs) and resource documentation, but valid files do not ensure that these artifacts describe the same objects. Treating the release as a data product, we audit HuggingBench (SIGIR 2025), a benchmark for recommending Hugging Face resources, through data validation, a replication of its eleven recommendation methods and controlled experiments with three training seeds. In three of its four external KGs, the files pass key and range checks but violate the item-entity identity constraint on which KG recommenders rely. Correcting this join improves every KG-based method in every seed, by up to 73% in mean Recall@10, and consistently reverses ten of 27 comparisons between KG configurations. The protocol matters as well: the 100-epoch budget ends before early stopping in seven to eight of 29 validation-selected settings, and 21 of 23 such setting-seed pairs improve with a longer budget. The released item text, which no reported method uses, is the strongest signal: closed-form linear models with text and the item graph exceed the best reported Recall@10 by 18% while fitting in minutes on a CPU. Checks of other recommendation releases show that individually valid releases of one dataset can use incompatible identifiers. We release corrected files, mappings, validators and logs, and derive practices for preserving identity and provenance across the artifacts of benchmarks and model lakes.
Machine Learning.comment: 12 pages, 10 tables, 2 figures. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23857277

Machine Learning.title: DualClusterNet: Personalized Pattern-Space Composition for Next-POI Recommendation
Machine Learning.summary: Next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation supports personalized place discovery on location-based Web platforms. Mobility routines can recur across users while being realized at different places and adapted to individual preferences. We present DualClusterNet, a causal sequential recommender that composes two population-shared prototype dictionaries. At each observed prefix, soft routers retrieve pattern and spatial mixtures; a factorized multiplicative interaction couples them, feature-wise affine modulation adapts the shared representation, and a separate user-conditioned branch with an additive--projective gate retains individual variation. The prediction head combines this representation with a learned first-order transition term and ranks the complete training POI vocabulary. We evaluate on NYC and TKY using a training-only vocabulary and an original-final-target protocol that neither bridges unknown POIs nor substitutes earlier targets. The available single-seed results show competitive full-candidate ranking, while controlled analyses support the contribution of the compositional and personalized branches. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DualClusterNet-F4EE/.

Machine Learning.title: Does the Trust Boundary Hold over Time? A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Receiver-Directed Federated Learning
Machine Learning.summary: In receiver-directed federated learning, each site draws a trust boundary. For every source and model component it judges, on its own data, whether the transfer helps (admit), harms (reject) or cannot yet be told (abstain). We ask whether this boundary holds over hundreds of rounds. Our benchmark has a federation of thirteen semi-synthetic sites, an exact oracle for every evaluated transfer, paired seeds, an attack protocol, fourteen methods over 600 rounds and Qwen3-1.7B LoRA sites over 500. The answer depends on which boundary is measured. Across 20 paired CPU seeds, a gate judging against a fixed reference better identified transfers useful relative to the site's starting model. Yet it admitted 29% of transfers harmful to the model the site now has. A gate judging against the current model admitted 2% of harmful transfers on that target in the CPU tier, but missed many transfers useful to the starting model. Two short propositions explain these distinct failures. We also evaluate a held out audit that leaves gate verdicts intact. After training, it decides whether each final model is deployed or the site falls back to local training, and reports admissions that have gone stale. With independent audit data its guarantees hold after any training history. At 600 rounds the audit deployed 65 to 72% of models, none with negative benefit on its target, and kept 98% of the gain. No stale report had the wrong sign in our runs. With 20,000 audit observations, a variance-adaptive bound found 99% of stale transfers that cost at least 0.01 in log loss. A common-target Qwen3 comparison on 60 selected transfers shows the same tension over 100 rounds. With 38% adversarial sites, FedFomo and CS-Gate were the only evaluated methods with positive mean gain in every honest group.
Machine Learning.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables. Code: https://github.com/tinaxu226/trust-boundary-benchmark (available upon acceptance)

Machine Learning.title: EMBERS: Empirically Motivated Robustness Testing of Deep Research Systems via Defect-Guided Fuzzing
Machine Learning.summary: Deep Research (DR) systems extend large language models into autonomous agents that decompose complex information needs, iteratively search the web, and synthesize evidence to answer challenging questions. However, their multi-stage execution may introduce robustness risks, as variations in user questions or intermediate search inputs may propagate across research stages and lead to incorrect answers. Existing evaluations focus on task-solving capabilities or robustness against external evidence disturbances, leaving intrinsic weaknesses in DR execution insufficiently explored. Thus, we conduct an empirical study of 1,932 execution trajectories from three representative DR systems and identify nine recurring defect categories across subquestion formulation, online search, and final reasoning. Guided by these findings, we propose EMBERS, an empirically motivated, defect-guided fuzzing framework for robustness testing of DR systems. Starting from correctly answered seed questions, EMBERS generates stage-targeted test inputs using defect-guided mutation, web-search-assisted fidelity assurance, and diversity-aware seed maintenance. Experiments across 16 framework--model--dataset settings show that EMBERS achieves 3.21 times the failure-discovery throughput of the strongest baseline under identical testing budgets. Human and LLM-assisted evaluations demonstrate that most generated inputs preserve the original information need and necessary contextual constraints. Moreover, model fine-tuning experiments show consistent-answer performance improvement, highlighting their value for robustness testing and model improvement.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LIPAR: Training-free Latent Inter-Frame Pruning with Attention Recovery
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Video generation enables text-to-video synthesis, video editing, and motion-controlled content creation. However, current video generation models suffer from high computational latency, rendering true real-time capabilities infeasible for downstream tasks. We address this limitation by exploiting the temporal redundancy inherent in video latent patches. To this end, we propose the Latent Inter-frame Pruning with Attention Recovery (LIPAR) framework, which detects and skips recomputing duplicated latent patches. Additionally, we introduce a novel Attention Recovery mechanism that approximates the attention values of pruned tokens, thereby removing visual artifacts arising from naively applying the pruning method. Empirically, our method increases generation throughput by $1.45\times$, on average achieving 12.2 FPS on an NVIDIA A6000 compared to the baseline 8.4 FPS. The proposed method does not compromise generation quality and can be seamlessly integrated with Diffusion Transformer without additional training. Our approach effectively bridges the gap between traditional compression algorithms and modern generative pipelines.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: [Re] Pure Noise to the Rescue of Insufficient Data
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We examine the main claims of Zada, Benou, and Irani (2021), which states that in an image classification task with imbalanced training data, (i) using pure noise to augment minority-class images encourages generalization by improving minority-class accuracy. This method is paired with (ii) a new batch normalization layer that normalizes noise images using affine parameters learned from natural images, which improves the model's performance. Moreover, (iii) this improvement is robust to varying levels of data augmentation. Finally, the authors propose that (iv) adding pure noise images can improve classification even on balanced training data. We implemented the training pipeline from the description of the paper using PyTorch and integrated authors' code snippets for sampling pure noise images and batch normalizing noise and natural images separately. We reproduced the main claims that (i) oversampling with pure noise improves generalization by improving the minority-class accuracy, (ii) the proposed batch normalization (BN) method outperforms baselines, (iii) and this improvement is robust across data augmentations. Our results also support that (iv) adding pure noise images can improve classification on balanced training data. However, additional experiments suggest that the performance improvement from OPeN may be more orthogonal to the improvement caused by a bigger network or more complex data augmentation.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Reproducibility study of Zada et al. (arXiv:2112.08810). Published in ReScience C 9(2), #45 (2023), ML Reproducibility Challenge 2022. 15 pages. Code: https://github.com/seungjaeryanlee/pure-noise

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DriftingPlanner: Drifting Generative Models for One-Step Trajectory Planning in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: End-to-end planners decode the ego trajectory either by coordinate regression, which is fast but blends plausible maneuvers into one trajectory that may follow none of them, or by diffusion and flow matching, which model the trajectory distribution but need several inference steps. Drifting models move this iteration into training: a one-step generator learns to follow an attraction--repulsion field between generated and ground-truth samples. Drifting was developed for class-conditional image generation, where every class supplies many positive samples. In planning, every scene is its own condition. Pooling scenes would attract the generated trajectories of one scene to the ground truth of unrelated scenes, whereas computing the field per scene leaves a single positive, the expert trajectory. Mutual repulsion then holds the generated trajectories on a shell around it, so any single generated trajectory deviates from the ground truth. We present DriftingPlanner, a trajectory planner trained with the drifting loss alone, without any coordinate regression term. It computes the field per scene and removes the shell at inference: it decodes every noise vector together with its negation in one batched pass, and averaging each antithetic pair cancels the linear part of the displacement from the shell center. On NAVSIM navtest, DriftingPlanner reaches a state-of-the-art 93.75 PDMS, and with single-step inference its drifting decoder comes within 0.13 PDMS of the best diffusion or flow matching setting, which needs ten inference steps.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: StreamClarify: Proactive Clarification for Grounded Streaming Video Question Answering
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Streaming video question answering (QA) requires real-time reasoning over continuous video streams under strict latency and active-context budgets. Current streaming vision-language models (VLMs) often give confident yet ungrounded answers when queries are ambiguous or have false premises, or when relevant visual evidence is no longer in the active context. Proactive clarification can help, but must satisfy the same latency and memory constraints. We present StreamClarify, a training-free framework for grounded streaming QA that combines a pre-answer uncertainty check with hierarchical memory. The check uses the entropy of a binary pre-answer judgment as a lightweight uncertainty score to decide whether to answer directly or request clarification. To support re-answering, a temporal-pyramid KV cache maintains a bounded active visual context, while a CPU-side semantic retrieval archive provides access to historical frames. We further construct StreamClarify-QA, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,837 QA pairs from StreamBench and OVO-Bench, spanning standard, referential ambiguity, and unanswerable scenarios. Across three VLM backbones, StreamClarify improves Macro accuracy by up to 8.2 points over backbone-matched baselines. At comparable trigger rates, entropy-based selection achieves more than 18 points higher precision than random selection in identifying initially incorrect answers. Under oracle user guidance, clarification improves Macro accuracy by up to 3.5 points. We also report a controlled, oracle-assisted Qwen3-VL simulation on Ambiguous QA with generated questions and referent-only user replies, where the entropy-gated condition improves accuracy by 8.3 points.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Context-Shielded Backdoor Attack against Large Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) routinely use inference-time visual-token compression to prune hundreds of patch tokens down to a compact budget. Existing LVLM backdoors fire whenever a triggered image appears, whereas prior deployment-triggered attacks activate only when model weights are quantized or pruned. However, conventional LVLM backdoors exhibit nearly 100% attack success rate (ASR) under full-token inference, immediately exposing compromised checkpoints during pre-deployment auditing. We reveal context stripping: surrounding clean visual tokens suppress an embedded trigger at full length, whereas token pruning strips this context away and activates the backdoor. Motivated by this finding, we propose StripWake, a projector-only backdoor that remains dormant under full-token auditing yet activates across unseen compressors. Specifically, StripWake pairs clean-supervised full-token views with target-supervised randomized compressed views, and aligns early visual attention with a frozen benign teacher to preserve clean utility. On LLaVA-1.5-7B across nine unseen compressors, StripWake stays dormant at 0.4% full-token ASR yet achieves 94.0%-99.7% compressed ASR across five primary compressors without CIDEr loss.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DuoGesture: Motion-Grounded Semantic Conditioning and Biomechanical Beat Priors for Co-Speech Gesture Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Co-speech gesture generation requires both semantic expressivity and biomechanically plausible rhythmic motion. Existing holistic gesture models mix lexically grounded semantic gestures with frequent prosody-aligned beat gestures. This limits semantic grounding, speech-motion alignment, and kinematic smoothness. We propose DuoGesture, a neuro-inspired and biomechanically informed approach that decomposes co-speech gesture synthesis into semantic and beat streams. The two streams are coordinated by a Semantic Variational Information Bottleneck, a stochastic frame-level gate that learns when semantic gestures should override rhythmic beat motion. The semantic stream is controlled by Motion-Grounded Semantic Conditioning, which replaces purely linguistic word embeddings with motion-language representations to provide motion-aligned semantic priors for long-tailed lexical triggers of gestures. The beat stream is further regularised by an Inertial Beat Prior, an anthropometry-weighted arm-chain module that reduces jitter and improves rhythmic consistency without constraining semantic frames. Objective evaluations and subjective experiments show that DuoGesture outperforms strong baselines, while component ablations confirm the complementary roles of semantic grounding, stochastic stream selection, and biomechanical regularisation. We encourage readers to view our demos and qualitative illustrations, which are available on the project page: https://ferdinandpaar.github.io/DuoGesture/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Can MLLMs Perceive and Describe Medical Image Quality Beyond Scores?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Medical Image Quality Assessment (IQA) serves as a critical safety gate for clinical AI, yet existing approaches rely on scalar metrics that fail to capture the descriptive, expert-like evaluation process central to clinical practice. We introduce MedQ-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for language-based medical IQA evaluation with MLLMs, establishing a perception--description paradigm across 5 imaging modalities and over 40 quality attributes. The benchmark comprises two complementary tasks: MedQ-Perception probes low-level visual attribute discrimination via 2,600 expert-annotated perceptual queries; MedQ-Description covers both no-reference and comparison description sub-tasks with 708 expert-annotated samples, evaluated through a four-dimensional judging protocol. Comprehensive evaluation of 23 state-of-the-art MLLMs reveals that current models exhibit only preliminary and unstable capabilities, and highlights the urgent need for targeted optimization of MLLMs in medical IQA. Project & Dataset: https://github.com/liujiyaoFDU/MedQ-Bench

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Reproducing INP-Former: Reconstructing Intrinsic Normal Prototypes for Industrial Anomaly Detection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We reproduce the central claims of INP-Former, a reconstruction-based method for multi-class industrial anomaly detection. INP-Former extracts Intrinsic Normal Prototypes (INPs) from each test image and uses them to guide a decoder that reconstructs normal features, without a stored memory bank. Using the authors' released code, we reproduce the reported performance on MVTec AD and VisA and extend the evaluation to MVTec AD 2, where image AUROC with the default settings is 63.4, compared with 99.7 on MVTec AD. On MVTec AD, a five-seed ablation shows that most of the performance comes from the INP mechanism, while the two auxiliary losses add small changes whose direction depends on the metric. A paired comparison with both losses disabled confirms the benefit of INP on MVTec AD 2. The default of six prototypes transfers less well: the plateau beyond four prototypes reproduces on MVTec AD and VisA, but on MVTec AD 2 a single prototype outperforms six in AU-PRO on the public split and on both hidden test splits. We also measure practical trade-offs in resolution, backbone size, training length, and LoRA adaptation, and examine performance by defect size, lighting condition, and a stricter AU-PRO limit. Several conclusions from the original benchmarks, including the default prototype count, do not carry over to harder data. Code: https://github.com/garasnote/Repro-INPFormer
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Reproducibility study. 12 pages of main text (excluding references and appendix), 14 tables. Code available at https://github.com/garasnote/Repro-INPFormer

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Modeling Fat-shift for Improved Head Segmentation from MRI Scans using a Probabilistic Model
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Personalized computational head models for biophysical simulations rely on accurate whole-head segmentations from T1-weighted (T1w) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. While T1w scans provide excellent contrast for intracranial anatomy, extracerebral tissues have partly almost no signal (compact bone) and also suffer from the so-called chemical shift artifact, which affects the fatty tissues in MRI and causes them to spatially shift in the frequency encoding direction of the scan. This artifact occurs primarily in two structures of the head: the spongy bone, a fatty compartment inside the compact bone, and the subcutaneous fat, located directly underneath the skin. The frequency-encoding direction is often set in the superior-inferior direction, causing the fatty tissues to shift down and, as a result, making the skull appear thinner than it actually is. Existing segmentation methods do not model this artifact, consequently leading to inaccurate labeling of the skull and scalp, which introduces a bias in biophysical simulations. The direction and magnitude of the fat-shift can be determined from the scan parameters, thus making it possible to explicitly model the shift and to recover the correct anatomy. This study introduces a probabilistic model that uses variational inference to segment head and brain structures from a T1w scan while accounting for the fat-shift artifact. The proposed Fat-shift-informed Label Optimization of the Whole head (FLOW) method reconstructs extracerebral anatomy more accurately than a fat-shift-agnostic segmentation approach while maintaining high segmentation accuracy in all other structures. FLOW-based fat-shift corrected segmentations significantly reduce bias in electric field simulations compared to a segmentation method that does not model the shift.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LPLCv2: An Expanded Dataset for Fine-Grained License Plate Legibility Classification
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Modern Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) systems achieve outstanding performance in controlled, well-defined scenarios. However, large-scale real-world usage remains challenging due to low-quality imaging devices, compression artifacts, and suboptimal camera installation. Identifying illegible license plates (LPs) has recently become feasible through a dedicated benchmark; however, its impact has been limited by its small size and annotation errors. In this work, we expand the original benchmark to over three times the size with two extra capture days, revise its annotations and introduce novel labels. LP-level annotations include bounding boxes, text, and legibility level, while vehicle-level annotations comprise make, model, type, and color. Image-level annotations feature camera identity, capture conditions (e.g., rain and faulty cameras), acquisition time, and day ID. We present a novel training procedure featuring an Exponential Moving Average-based loss function and a refined learning rate scheduler, addressing common mistakes in testing. These improvements enable a baseline model to achieve an 89.5% F1-score on the test set, considerably surpassing the previous state of the art. We further introduce a novel protocol to explicitly addresses camera contamination between training and evaluation splits, where results show a small impact. Dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/lmlwojcik/LPLCv2-Dataset.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Vision-Language Models Are Joint Denoisers in Robotic Action Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) models cascade pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with diffusion action experts, but typically restrict the VLM to providing static conditioning. This separation limits how much pretrained perception and reasoning can guide action generation, especially in out-of-distribution settings. We introduce JADE, a Joint Action DEnoiser that enables the VLM and action expert to jointly refine actions. Our key insight is that structured action latents allow the VLM to read the current noisy action together with visual observations and language instructions. At every denoising step, the VLM contextualizes the noisy action and guides the action expert through gated cross-attention, so that its guidance evolves with the action being generated. We further supervise the VLM to recover clean action latents from noisy ones, which gives it a direct action-learning signal and couples perception with control. Additionally, joint denoising enables JADE to generate actions with fewer sampling steps, helping offset the additional cost of VLM participation. An adaptive step-size schedule further balances task performance and inference latency. On RoboDojo, JADE achieves an average success rate of 12.67%, the highest among the evaluated $π_{0.5}$-based methods, and is competitive with recent VLA and WAM foundation models pretrained at scale. It also improves performance on RoboTwin 2.0 and raises the average success rate across four real-world bimanual tasks by 20.8 percentage points compared with $π_{0.5}$.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Disentangling Perception and Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs via Reward Design
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has driven major gains in LLM reasoning, and it is intuitive to assume this recipe will transfer well to multimodal models. However, multimodal models do two things: first, perceive what is in an image, then reason about what it implies. Because these stages are graded jointly, it is hard to tell how much room reasoning alone has to grow. We study this on algorithmic visual puzzles, where both components are necessary and show that perception, not reasoning, is the binding constraint. Replacing images with simple textual descriptions raises performance by over 20 points on average for Claude models. We then evaluate six reward designs aimed at inducing visual grounding during reasoning without chain-of-thought supervision. Training Qwen-2.5-VL-7B with GRPO, reward design induces long, structured reasoning with self-reflection and visual references, yielding a 5.56-point gain over the base model. These gains are, however, uneven; no single reward improves all categories, and rewards with verifiable accuracy signals trade cross-domain transfer for in-domain accuracy. These results point to perception-aware reward design as a path forward, so that signals correct perception at its source rather than the reasoning that inherits its errors.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Vehicle speed dataset for the major European road network derived from Sentinel-2 imagery, 2022-2026
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The dataset provides individual vehicle speed observations on European E-roads: motorways, trunk roads, primary and secondary roads, as tagged in OpenStreetMap as e-road, for the years 2022-2026. Speeds are derived from Copernicus Sentinel-2 Level-2A satellite optical imagery using a processing pipeline that exploits the short, well-characterized acquisition delays between the blue (B02_10m), green (B03_10m), and red bands (B04_10m) of the Sentinel-2 push-broom instrument. A moving vehicle appears at slightly displaced positions in the three bands, forming a moving echo. The detected displaced intensity peaks are linked into per-vehicle trajectories through a prediction-and-matching procedure. The resulting displacements are converted into ground speeds using publicly accessible inter-band time delays. Each record contains the trajectory geometry, per-channel displacements and headings, internal quality indicators, the estimated speed, the acquisition timestamp, and the source Sentinel-2 product identifier. The dataset is distributed as GeoPackage files, with one record per detected vehicle, and can support studies of traffic patterns, speed behavior, transport modeling, and the calibration of road network attributes at a continental scale.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MemoCare: An Interactive Multimodal Mobile System for Automated Cognitive Screening
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: MemoCare is a React Native mobile system for automated multimodal cognitive screening in English and Vietnamese. It integrates speech, temporal and spatial orientation, touchscreen interaction, and visuoconstruction. Google Speech-to-Text transcripts are scored with deterministic, task-specific rules. GPS-grounded current and historical administrative names support location scoring, touch events verify actions, and lightweight convolutional neural networks evaluate drawings. A separate model provides visual interpretation. Software verification passed 151/151 predefined language, spatial-answer, and touch-scoring regression cases and 48/48 fixed-coordinate spatial tests across four countries. Transcript-based tests exclude speech recognition accuracy. On a locked 71-image test set, validation-selected ShuffleNetV2 x1.5 achieved 91.33% mean balanced accuracy and 78.87% exact three-criterion accuracy. Four clinician co-authors rated the workflow (pooled median 4/5 across eight criteria; item medians 3-4.5), highlighting improvements needed in speech handling, response acceptance, and result transparency. The workflow automatically produces item-level and total scores.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Accepted at the demonstration track at MMM 2027

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SemICP: Semantic Non-Rigid Point Cloud Registration with Elastic Energy Regularization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
Purpose: Accurate point cloud registration is essential in computer-aided interventions (CAI) to align multi-modal medical images for intraoperative guidance. Classical methods, such as Iterative Closest Point (ICP), remain attractive for their explainability and minimal training requirements, but typically ignore anatomical semantics and biomechanical properties during regularization.
  Methods: We present Semantic ICP (SemICP), a novel non-rigid point cloud registration framework that combines semantically informed point matching with linear elastic energy regularization. Semantic labels are used to improve correspondence matching by constraining correspondences to be anatomically consistent. A novel control-point deformation representation with linear-elastic energy regularization is introduced to encourage biomechanically plausible deformations. SemICP was evaluated on a simulation phantom and four datasets against established baselines. It was also tested with labels from AI-based segmentation in a fully automatic segmentation-registration pipeline.
  Results: On the finite element phantom, SemICP recovered 86% of the interior displacement from surface observations alone. On the real datasets, SemICP achieved the lowest target registration error on Liver MR-US and the lowest surface distances on TORS, and ranked second on AbdominalMR-CT and HippocampusMR, where NR-ICP achieved lower surface distances. The fully automatic registration pipeline was shown to be effective for US-MR registration and to improve the alignment of expert-annotated structures.
  Conclusion: SemICP improves interior accuracy at competitive surface accuracy by combining semantic correspondence constraints and linear energy regularization. Combined with AI-based segmentation, SemICP provides an effective pipeline for multi-modal registration in CAI.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: 3D-USE: From Image-Level to Scene-Level Underwater Enhancement
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Underwater scene reconstruction from degraded views can preserve visual degradation. Since paired enhanced 3D references are hard to obtain in real ocean scenes, underwater 3D methods largely rely on physics-based restoration. However, separating object radiance from medium effects is ill-posed and may leave residual artifacts. In contrast, we formulate underwater scene enhancement as learning the desired appearance of the scene and propose a two-stage framework called 3D-USE. Stage 1 builds a medium-aware Gaussian scene with MediumRBF, sharing medium estimates across nearby views and establishing stable geometry and visibility. Using a prior learned from external 2D enhancement pairs, Stage 2 applies Appearance Transition Consensus (ATC) to calibrate and aggregate view-wise appearance changes, defining the desired scene-level appearance transformation. Finally, an Underwater Bilateral Appearance Field (U-BAF) jointly adjusts object radiance and medium appearance to produce coherent enhanced appearance across viewpoints. Experiments show that 3D-USE improves novel-view enhancement and cross-view consistency while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality. The project page and code are available at https://bilityniu.github.io/3D-USE/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: VOICE: A Vision-Omics Foundation Model Integrating Direct and Retrieval-Based Prediction of In-situ Single-Cell Gene Expression
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Spatial transcriptomics can resolve gene expression at single-cell resolution, but it is costly, limited to targeted panels of a few hundred to a few thousand genes, and applicable to only a small number of samples. H&E imaging, by contrast, is cheap and collected routinely at scale. This makes predicting single-cell expression directly from morphology a practical way to bring molecular analysis to large tissue archives. We therefore present VOICE, a multimodal foundation model that predicts single-cell gene expression from H&E images using paired Xenium data. VOICE first aligns cell centered H&E morphology from a pathology foundation model with single-cell expression embeddings from a transcriptome foundation model, trained using contrastive learning over 23 million cells. Next it predicts expression through two branches. One branch directly regresses expression from morphology. The other branch retrieves measured expression from similar reference cells, recovering genes that do not have morphological signal. Because genes vary in morphological predictability, VOICE fuses the two branches with a per-gene weight. After training, VOICE generalizes to heldout patients, slides, and partially overlapping gene panels from Xenium, and it consistently outperforms prior single-cell expression prediction methods on seven metrics.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SHield: Watermarking 4D Gaussian Splatting via Spherical Harmonic Coefficient Perturbation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) models are computationally expensive to train but distributed as easily copied parameter files. Existing watermarks protect these assets by fine-tuning the scene against a neural decoder to extract bit strings from rendered video, a heavy process vulnerable to the temporal dynamics of dynamic scenes. However, if the threat model targets the redistributed file itself, verification can be vastly simplified. Because the canonical Spherical-Harmonic (SH) coefficients of 4DGS are time- and view-invariant, parameter-space perturbations can be recovered via deterministic arithmetic. We propose **SHield**, the first non-blind, decoder-free watermarking approach that natively embeds full-resolution RGB images into 4DGS files. SHield tiles a zero-mean payload across the SH coefficients of a key-selected Gaussian subset, applying a brief anchored optimization to preserve visual fidelity. To verify ownership, it geometrically re-associates the key using canonical Gaussian centres to survive file tampering and recovers the payload in closed form. Across 30 scenes (D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, DyNeRF), SHield guarantees near-perfect payload recovery (Pearson $r \geq 0.991$) on all 150 tested models with a mean rendering penalty of $\leq 0.13$~dB. Held-out evaluation yields perfect detection on 400 true trials and zero false positives across $1{,}600$ wrong-subset null trials. We also strictly bound the method's robustness: SHield survives INT8 quantization and $30\%$ opacity pruning for the image payload, and on aggressive SH-degree-1 truncation bit payloads are still decodable.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Simplifying, Scaling, and Saturating Flow Matching for Cell Microscopy
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Flow-matching generative models are increasingly used to simulate cell responses to biological perturbations. However, the design space for building such models is large and underexplored. We systematically analyse the design space of flow matching models for cell microscopy images, finding that many popular techniques can add unnecessary complexity and may even hurt performance. We develop a simple, stable, and scalable recipe which we use to train our generative microscopy model. We scale training compute to an order of magnitude larger than prior methods, saturating existing public benchmarks with approximately two-fold FID and ten-fold KID improvements over prior methods. We report an extended battery of metrics, finding that improved evaluation encoders can alleviate the saturation problem. Our methods represent progress towards high-fidelity virtual microscopy assays for tasks such as virtual screening, batch effect correction, and data enrichment.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Updated version presented at NeurIPS ML4SpatialBio 2026 workshop (Oral)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Language models' abilities to interpret tasks and generate programs offer a promising basis for 3D spatial reasoning. Yet following spatial instructions in 3D scenes requires programs to construct geometric references that language leaves implicit. In this work, we introduce VoxProg, which formulates 3D object placement through voxel programming: a language model translates task interpretations into executable programs over local voxel views of scene surfaces. Because these views index surface geometry on regular grids with explicit coordinates and neighborhood relations, an evidence program can isolate task-relevant regions and boundaries directly from scene meshes, and a downstream pose program can measure the resulting geometry to compute a target $SE(3)$ pose. Visual and numerical feedback from execution lets the model inspect intermediate selections and candidate placements to iteratively revise its code. To evaluate open-ended placement across functional use, geometric fit, and contextual arrangements, we introduce the 71-task VoxProg-Bench benchmark along with an evaluation suite pairing perceptual Intent Alignment and 3D Physical Validity. Across VoxProg-Bench and external benchmarks, VoxProg consistently outperforms relation-based, keypoint-based, and mesh-based baselines.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: GESTALT: Fast, Generalizable Histopathology Image Synthesis from Gene Expression with Pretrained Pathology Foundation Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Spatial transcriptomics measures gene expression while preserving where each cell sits in the tissue. The inverse, what a given transcriptomic state looks like, is less explored but equally useful: it lets researchers visualize the morphological consequence of a molecular state and interpret a spatial assay's molecular calls against real tissue structure. GeneFlow, the current state of the art on the Xenium gene expression-to-image benchmark, trains a model from scratch, incurring a high cost on every new target dataset it is applied to. We instead propose GESTALT, which reformulates gene expression-to-image synthesis as predicting a pathology foundation model's image embedding. A lightweight gene-token transformer predicts this embedding from multi-cell gene expression, and a frozen or LoRA-adapted diffusion decoder (PixCell) renders it as an image. Because this visual knowledge is reused rather than relearned, GESTALT trains in a fraction of the time. In both multi-cell and single-cell settings, our method outperforms the SoTA on perceptual metrics across all three Xenium datasets. Beyond improved image quality, GESTALT natively synthesizes at 1024 x 1024, and is evaluated in three generalization settings: zero-shot transfer across gene panels and datasets, held-out patients and disease states, and transfer across studies and tissue sources. Coupled with a statistical model of spatial expression, GESTALT also provides, to our knowledge, the first paired synthesis of cell-resolved transcriptomic fields and tissue images with explicit control over cell type, density, and composition. Code is available at https://github.com/trongnhandev1011/Gestalt.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted at WACV 2027. 10 pages (8 main paper + 2 references), 4 figures. 8 pages of supplementary material

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: What Does a Safety Label Measure? Auditing Situational-Safety Benchmarks for Multimodal LLMs
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Situational-safety benchmarks label each scene SAFE or UNSAFE and score a multimodal large language model (MLLM) against that label, usually by judging its free-form answer, and these scores guide deployment. We ask what such a label measures. A label score can come from the scene, the request or the benchmark's own files. We propose the Benchmark Card, seven measured fields that tell them apart, and fill it for six benchmarks. Only MSSBench chat leaks the label through its image files: image size alone reaches 82.3% accuracy, matching or beating six of seven commercial models. Elsewhere the signal outside the scene comes from design. In MOSSBench the item partition fixes the label, and on HoliSafe the request alone ranks pairs about as well as the scene. On our corrected chat split, the size rule falls to chance. We then introduce the Spot-Stop decomposition, which compares ranking with labelling on pairs of a safe and an unsafe scene. It splits the gap above a label-swap null into three parts: a threshold part, overlap between safe and unsafe scores, and order that holds only within a pair. Most of fourteen open MLLMs rank better than they label, beyond what their AUROC predicts. On chat, one shared threshold repairs a third to a half of the excess, and label-free recentering recovers it on balanced batches. Recentering on unlabelled scenes of the same situation improves ranking on VSCBench for 13 of 14 models.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games. We study cross-game streaming commentary, in which a model trained on one game commentates games it has never seen, and find that current commentators transfer their timing but not their knowledge of the game world. We propose StreamDuo, which pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that reads the wiki of the game being played. When the commentator sees something it cannot name, it sends the current frames, and the research agent returns a few wiki entries two seconds later while the stream continues. We train only the commentator, on a single game, in two stages. Information-gain labels teach it to ask only where an answer would help it say what the human caster said, and on-policy self-distillation from a copy of itself that sees the ideal answer teaches it to use noisy answers. Trained on Baldur's Gate 3 and tested on ten unseen games, StreamDuo raises entity recall from 0.082 to 0.116 over Proact-VL trained on the same data, cuts source-game leakage from 9.9% to 1.0%, and achieves the best timing and the highest judged liveliness and overall quality among streaming models.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Pop Goes the Verifier: Phoneme-Targeted Data Poisoning of Voice Liveness Detection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Many Automated Speaker Verification Systems (ASVs) commonly employ liveliness detection techniques, such as VoicePop, which identify genuine speech by analyzing low- frequency pop bursts from plosive phonemes using Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (GFCC) and an SVM classifier. While effective against traditional replay attacks, such systems are vulnerable to data poisoning techniques. Prior work shows that broadly applied SyntheticPop attacks can collapse model to accuracy to as low as 14.01% using only 20% poisoned samples, but the resulting artifacts are easily detectable when visualizing the waveform energies. This paper introduces Pop Goes the Verifier, a stealthier phoneme injection poisoning attack. By leveraging FastSpeech 2 (FS2) with a modified HiFi-GAN vocoder, we inject localized pop bursts at plosive phoneme locations and overlay subtle Gaussian noise to reduce the visibility of injected artifacts in waveform and spectrogram analysis. Using the ASVSpoof 2019 as the dataset, we observe that the approach achieves a moderate poisoning attack while providing greater resistance to signal-level inspection than the original SyntheticPop attack.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted at IEEE International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB) 2026

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: QVR3D: Query-Guided Visual Reasoning for Training-Free 3D Grounding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3D visual grounding localizes objects in 3D scenes from natural language descriptions, requiring reasoning over semantics, spatial relationships, and multi-view observations. Training-free approaches avoid costly annotations but often rely on explicit scene transformation or scene-level frame selection, which may waste limited visual capacity on query-irrelevant regions. We observe that effective grounding should prioritize observations that provide evidence for the query rather than uniformly represent the entire scene. Based on this insight, we introduce QVR3D, a query-guided visual reasoning framework that operates on RGB-D observations using off-the-shelf foundation models. QVR3D combines Query-Guided Maximum Coverage (QGMC) for selecting complementary query-relevant views with Grounding Probability Estimation (GPE) that integrates instance confidence, attribute consistency, and relationship consistency. The framework supports both single- and multi-object grounding without task-specific adaptation. Experiments on ScanRefer and Nr3D achieve state-of-the-art zero-shot performance, while QGMC also improves frame efficiency across multiple 3D vision-language tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/jwliao1209/QVR3D.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CuPH: Parallel Cubical Persistent Homology via Level-Synchronous Component Tracking
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Persistent homology (PH) is a mathematically principled multi-scale topological descriptor of shape and connectivity in data. It is widely applied in image classification, segmentation, and shape analysis across medical and aerial imaging, providing structural information that pixel-wise deep learning may overlook. Standard cubical PH decomposes an image into cubical cells (vertices, edges, and squares) and reduces them sequentially in filtration order. This sequential reduction has $Θ(n)$ parallel depth for an $n$-pixel image, limiting within-image GPU parallelism and constraining its use in topology-aware deep learning. We introduce CuPH, a GPU-based parallel algorithm for computing cubical PH on 2D images that operates directly on pixels rather than cubical cells. CuPH buckets pixels by filtration values, activates them with a level-synchronous sweep, and tracks connected components with a lock-free union-find method. We prove that CuPH produces persistence diagrams identical to standard cubical PH on integer inputs, with a stability bound for floating-point inputs. CuPH reduces parallel depth from $Θ(n)$ to $O(L\log n)$ for an image with $L$ intensity levels. We implement the level sweep as a single CUDA kernel, eliminating cross-level kernel-launch overhead. Empirically, CuPH is $18.6$--$99.6\times$ faster than the existing GPU baseline (CMP). As a drop-in PH backend, CuPH accelerates topology-aware classification ($4.2$--$16.7\times$) and segmentation ($8.3$--$44\times$) while preserving accuracy. It also enables computing full-image PH losses on high-resolution images, improving segmentation Dice by $2.2$--$4.6$ points over patch-local PH baselines and accelerating training by $25$--$31\times$.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Grounding Across Views: Cross-View Referring Reasoning for Visual Grounding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Cross-view object geo-localization (CVOGL) aims to localize a target in a satellite image from an observation captured under another viewpoint. Existing methods typically specify the query with a click point or bounding box, marking the target region but underusing the semantic attributes and relations conveyed by natural language. Moreover, referring expressions are often viewpoint-dependent, making query-view descriptions difficult to ground directly in the satellite image. In this paper, we formulate cross-view visual grounding (CVVG), extending conventional point- or box-prompted CVOGL to instance grounding jointly guided by a referring expression and a visual exemplar. We present GAV (Grounding Across Views), a view-aware framework for selectively transferring visual and linguistic evidence across views. Its core is view-aware referring reasoning: target-centered descriptions are derived from the marked query image, checked for target-category consistency, and augmented with a direction-free role cue. Exemplar prompting, cross-view alignment, and scene-level discrimination ground this semantic evidence in a satellite instance. GAV achieves a new state of the art on MoP-UAV with 62.55% Acc@0.5. We also introduce CVOGL-Text, a benchmark for text-guided grounding from street- and drone-view queries to satellite images. GAV outperforms the click-point baseline by 7.09 and 6.79 Acc@0.25 points on the street- and drone-view splits, respectively, demonstrating robustness to larger viewpoint gaps. The code and annotations will be publicly released.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Adaptive Land Units from Earth Embeddings
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Modeling land use starts with a choice of spatial units, typically a regular grid of pixels whose resolution is set by the spatial detail the process requires and, often more critically, by the computational budget. With Earth observation data more abundant than ever, we ask whether good land units can instead emerge from the data itself. To do that, we cluster AlphaEarth embeddings with a parallel Bayesian hierarchical clustering into adaptive land units, large where the land is uniform and small where it is highly heterogeneous. Using Denmark as a case study, we turn 402M land pixels into 1.27M newly defined units, about 320 times fewer, without any labels (i.e., unsupervised), making it possible to fit the whole country on a single consumer-grade GPU. Importantly, these units describe the land well, as a regular grid needs about 5 times as many cells to match them against land-use labels, and about 4 times as many against the declared crop of every field. Compared to clustering the satellite images themselves, the embeddings need half the units for the same purity. But more notably, they work as modeling units. Land-use maps learned on them are within a few points of accuracy of pixel models at a small fraction of the cost, and they make whole-country land-use estimates with reliable uncertainty possible in under a minute, where the same model on pixels does not even fit in device memory.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables, including supplementary material. Code and data at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23836328

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ExeWorldBench: Benchmarking Code-Based Executable 3D World Modeling
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Coding agents are increasingly evolving beyond reproducing what a world looks like toward constructing executable worlds that capture how a world works. This shift calls for executable world modeling, which integrates two core capabilities: world understanding, reasoning about the underlying structural, mechanical, and causal principles of a world, and executable realization, translating that understanding into a code-based system whose behavior emerges from physical interactions. However, existing benchmarks provide only fragmented evaluations centered on physical reasoning, visual fidelity, or behavioral correctness, leaving the integration of these capabilities insufficiently assessed. To bridge this gap, we introduce ExeWorldBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark to comprehensively evaluate world understanding and executable realization through code-based 3D world construction. ExeWorldBench comprises three progressively challenging tasks: Mechanism Executability, which evaluates the realization of individual mechanisms from visual observations; Compositional Executability, which extends to multi-stage systems with spatial, mechanical, and causal dependencies; and Intent-Driven Executable World Synthesis, which requires constructing executable worlds from high-level goals and physical requirements. Extensive experiments on frontier models reveal substantial limitations in executable world modeling, offering insights into the development of more physically grounded and causally coherent world construction systems.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Robust Pixel-wise Digital Image Correlation under Large Motions and Illumination Variations via a Global-to-Local Hybrid Neural Field
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Digital image correlation (DIC) is a widely used non-contact technique for full-field displacement measurement. Data-driven deep-learning DIC offers rapid inference but may generalize poorly to unseen speckle patterns, deformation modes, noise levels, and illumination conditions. Classical optimization-based DIC and recent image-constrained neural formulations avoid labeled displacement data, yet their convergence and accuracy remain vulnerable to initialization, large rigid-body motion, fine non-uniform deformation, and gray-value disturbances. This paper presents a global-to-local hybrid neural DIC framework for robust pixelwise measurement. Stage 1 estimates a dominant in-plane rigid transformation through coarse rotation search, phase correlation, and masked refinement, providing a reliable initialization under large translation and rotation. Stage 2 represents the residual displacement with a hybrid Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) and multilayer perceptron (MLP), and optimizes it using a valid-overlap, illumination-robust structural loss. The local gray-value model explicitly accommodates multiplicative and additive intensity changes. Simulated and real experiments demonstrate accurate and stable displacement recovery under noise, non-uniform deformation, large rotation, illumination variation, and degraded imaging conditions.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Stabilizing Camera-Controlled Novel View Synthesis at Inference Time
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Training-free, camera-controlled novel view synthesis from a single image using pre-trained video diffusion models often becomes unstable under large camera motion and long generation horizons. Existing approaches commonly combine several inference-time components, making it unclear which design choices are most important for stability. This work identifies the amount of camera motion handled by each diffusion pass as the main factor. CamTrol++ splits the camera path into passes that each cover at most a fixed rotation and generates them one after another, so that every pass stays within the range of motion the backbone handles well. A matched study, in which every setting is scored on the same poses of the same $60^\circ$ orbit, shows that geometric error grows steadily with the arc per pass, while a single SVD pass both loses geometry and tends to freeze the camera. Under one shared camera path, CamTrol++ achieves the lowest epipolar error and the best held-out 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction among CamTrol, NVS-Solver and WAVE, and reaches the quality of CamTrol with the same pass structure at least $3.2\times$ faster. On real RealEstate10K motion it matches CamTrol at half the run time (NVS-Solver is more faithful but $8\times$ slower). The same procedure also improves 3D reconstruction with a second video backbone, LTX-Video. Geometry-constrained spatial attention, color anchoring at pass boundaries and a registration-free warping pipeline that makes warping $6.1\times$ faster complete the framework. The method remains effective for 56-frame generation and under controlled depth corruption. These results show that careful control of camera motion at inference time can substantially improve the stability of camera-controlled novel view synthesis.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Efficient Image Denoising on Smartphone GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Image denoising is a fundamental problem in mobile photography. Despite a large number of solutions proposed for this task, the majority of them are trained on synthetically produced noisy images, and are additionally too computationally heavy for processing full-resolution images on mobile devices. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on constrained mobile hardware. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can denoise Full HD resolution photos while running on popular smartphone GPUs from Qualcomm and Arm. For this, the participants were provided with a large-scale dataset consisting of noisy-clean image pairs captured in the wild. The runtime of all models was evaluated on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Dimensity 9500 chipsets with the Adreno and Mali GPUs, respectively. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to perform high-quality image denoising under 100 milliseconds on both platforms while reaching a PSNR score of over 37 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: 4K Image Super-Resolution on Mobile NPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
